display.title: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev and the Three Din Torahs
display.summary_short: Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev attends the funeral of a rich man everyone called a miser, and explains with three din Torahs what a hidden tzaddik he was.
display.summary_long: Before the Rebbe Rashab's 160th birthday, the storyteller explains that Tomchei Temimim was founded to teach Chassidus and its way of seeing every Jew in a good light, as Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev did. When Shimon, a rich man thought to be a miser, passes away, the Chevra Kadisha wants to charge his family extra; the Berditchever forbids it and attends the funeral, and the whole town follows. Afterwards he tells three din Torahs. First, Shimon claimed to have found a merchant's lost money to save the fainting man's life, and refused repayment when the real finder came forward. Second, a poor man left town pretending to work for Shimon, and Shimon quietly paid the wife a weekly wage, refusing to be repaid. Third, a borrower named Hashem as his guarantor and came late to repay; Shimon said Hashem had already paid him through a good profit. The lesson: never judge a person from the outside.
display.lesson: Look at every Jew with a good eye; you never know the good a person does in secret.
